title: Tools and instruments
summary: Things built to do one job, and the words for them.

questions.clue: You look through this instrument to see things that are far too small for the naked eye.
questions.note: Micro means small and scope means to look at. A telescope does the opposite job, for things too far away.

questions.clue: This instrument has a magnetised needle that always settles pointing north.
questions.note: The same word also means the hinged instrument for drawing circles, which is why the clue mentions the needle and the north.

questions.clue: This is a tool for gripping and turning a nut or a bolt.
questions.note: Spanner is British and wrench is American. Both are accepted.

questions.clue: This is a cone-shaped tube used to pour liquid into a container with a narrow opening.
questions.note: The same word describes anything narrowing to a point, which is why a tornado is sometimes called a funnel cloud.

questions.clue: This piece of metal attracts iron and steel towards itself without touching them.
questions.note: The word comes from Magnesia, a region in ancient Greece where naturally magnetic rock was found.

questions.clue: This is a machine that makes holes by spinning a sharp bit round at speed.
questions.note: The same word is used for the practice of a routine, as in a fire drill, from the idea of repeated boring motion.

questions.clue: This has two rungs joined by steps and you climb it to reach something high.
questions.note: A ladder leans; a stepladder stands on its own with a hinge. The clue describes the ordinary leaning kind.

questions.clue: This instrument weighs things by comparing them, or by showing a number on a dial.
questions.note: British English usually says a pair of scales; American English says a scale. A balance is the older two-pan version.

questions.clue: This tool is a flat blade on a long handle, used for digging into soil.
questions.note: Strictly a spade cuts into ground and a shovel lifts loose material, but most speakers use the two words for each other.

questions.clue: This is the instrument a builder uses to check that a surface is perfectly horizontal.
questions.note: A bubble sits in a tube of liquid and rests in the centre only when the surface is flat, which is why it is called a spirit level.
